newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker, profit taken on spreads.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker, profit taken on spreads.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Wednesday, underperforming their U.S. counterparts as investors took profits on recent sharp gains and outperformance by Canadian bonds, analysts said.

"We expected, based on the run we've had over the last little while, to see some consolidation. So far that's pretty much what we've got," said Arve Bendiksrud, fixed-income analyst with TD Securities.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.52 to C$115.58 to yield 6.732 percent, while the U.S. 30-year benchmark bonds fell 4/32 to yield 6.45 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 28 basis points from 26 basis points at Tuesday's close.
"We have outperformed the U.S. for quite some time now, and without any events to trigger trading this week it probably was an opportune time to take profits," said Bendiksrud.

Canadian bonds have strengthened with U.S. Treasuries in recent weeks on speculation the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee would not raise rates when it met today. As a result the FOMC's decision to keep rates unchanged had little market impact.
Despite their weakness during today's session, Canadian bonds are expected to outperform U.S. Treasuries over the medium-term because of positive fundamentals such as low inflation, Bendiksrud said.
Analysts said investors are now looking ahead to the release of the Bank of Canada's semi-annual monetary policy report due out tomorrow, as well as details of next week's five year bond auction.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.34 to C$106.15 to yield 6.168 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.19 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to two basis points from six basis points at Tuesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.91 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.17 percent.
